messages:
alex: Heads-up — after today's rollout we see a sharp token/sec drop on continuous-batcher traffic (long-context convs). Started ~1779010500, spike after merge #4321. Notable queueing jitter and bigger tail latency.
priya: Can you drop the numbers and a short repro?
alex: Baselines: pre-merge sustained ~12k tokens/sec for the test harness. Post-merge ~7.8k, 35% drop. P95 latency up ~1.8x. Repro on canary with the same traffic pattern.
alex: Quick profiler dump from canary (short):
```
Flame: /proc/profile/2026-03-xx
- batcher::enqueue_lock ........ 38.2%\n- kernel_selector::choose_path . 21.5%\n- runtime::kernel_launch_sync .. 12.1%\n- kv_cache::lookup_collisions ... 8.7%\n- other (syscalls/IO) .......... 19.5%\n```
jason: That enqueue_lock number is huge. Did we change batching window or mutex contended path recently?
alex: Merge #4321 tweaked kernel selection to use per-shard sequence-length histogram + new batching window heuristic (adaptive_wait_ms). I suspect the selector is now doing heavier computation per-request and interacting badly with the batcher critical section.
emily: Looking at telemetry: sequence length distribution shifted on production (more long sequences). New selector checks histograms synchronously during enqueue to pick a kernel variant. If that code path is in the critical section, it'll serialize.
matt: Reproduced locally — with long ctx workload the selector does ~3-4 histogram traversals per enqueue. Here's the quick grep: `git show HEAD~1:runtime/kernel_selector.cpp` shows the new heuristics.
jason: Can we force the selector out of the hot path? Option A: move sampling to background + approximate cached variant. Option B: short-circuit selector on enqueue and pick fallback fast path.
perf-bot: CI perf alert: https://ci.internal/reports/merge-4321/perf-failure — builds show 30% token/sec regressions on the perf suite.
priya: Bisect plan: git bisect between pre-merge tag (v2026-03-01) and current. Prefer to test the selector-only changes first. Alex — can you run bisect + perf harness?
alex: Starting `git bisect` now against canary image. Will run perf harness with 10 minute steady-state runs.
(30m pass)
alex: Bisect narrowed to the kernel-selector patch set (the heuristics commit). Reverting locally the histogram-sync change restores previous tokens/sec.
emily: That aligns with the contention theory. Also saw slight increase in KV cache collision logs when selector spends longer in enq. Probably backlog grows and we miss prefix cache hits.
matt: Quick hotfix ready: set `batching.adaptive_wait_ms = 4` (was 12) and add an env `RUNTIME_KERNEL_SELECTOR_SYNC=0` to short-circuit heavy checks. Patch attached: `runtime: fast-path selector when in batch enqueue`
jason: Can we ship the env toggle as instant rollback if needed? Deploy-bot: Starting canary deploy of hotfix (env + reduced wait) to us-west-1 canaries.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for runtime-service on cluster inference-canary-2.
(10m)
alex: Canary metrics showing tokens/sec recovered to ~11.5k, p95 latency back near baseline. Queue depth and enqueue lock contention dropped in perf traces.
priya: Nice. Plan: revert the histogram-sync commit from main, or refactor to async sampling + cached decision. Revert seems safest for rollout.
jason: I can prepare the revert PR + post-merge follow-up that moves selection to background sampling with a windowed cache and lock-free fast path.
emily: Also add a guard in scheduler: if enqueue lock hold > 2ms, force fast kernel. That reduces tail risk.
alex: Action items: 1) jason open revert PR and mark as rollout-blocker; 2) emily add guard + telemetry to detect selector time in critical path; 3) matt prepare a follow-up that implements background histogram sampling; 4) priya coordinate revert release and postmortem.
priya: Agreed. I'll file the incident ticket and tag the release. Quick note: add a synthetic perf test for long-context continuous-batching so CI fails early if selector sync work regresses again.
perf-bot: Created perf regression ticket #PERF-2026-114 and added to release blocking list.
deploy-bot: Revert PR merged to main (hotfix). Rolling to remaining clusters now.
alex: After full rollout metrics look stable. tokens/sec back to pre-merge across clusters. Leaving postmortem/notes in #postmortems. Thanks team :thumbsup:
priya: Great follow-up work. We'll make heuristics async and add unit coverage for the selector.
